statements.t: • Adjusted Gross and Operating Margin Expansion Exceeded Our Outlook, Driven by Strong Full-Price Demand and Expense Discipline, More Than Offsetting Continued Investments in Marketing and Long-Term Growth Initiatives
"We delivered strong second quarter performance, enabling us to raise our Fiscal 2027 outlook once again," said Patrice Louvet, President and Chief Executive Officer.

"Through a dynamic global operating environment, we continue to invest in the strategic priorities that are bringing our Next Great Chapter: Drive plan to life — strengthening our brand desirability and delighting multi-generational customers in every geography around the world to drive sustainable long-term growth and value creation.
We remain confident in the strength of our brand, our teams and our diversified engines of growth through this fiscal year and beyond."
In the second quarter of Fiscal 2027, the Company had an effective tax rate of approximately 20% on a reported basis and 19% on an adjusted basis, in-line with its outlook.

The Company's outlook is based on its best assessment of the current geopolitical and macroeconomic environment, including tariffs, inflationary pressures and other consumer spending-related headwinds, global supply chain disruptions, and foreign currency volatility, among other factors.

For Fiscal 2027, the Company expects constant currency revenues to increase mid- to high-single digits to last year on a 52-week comparable basis, now centered around 6% to 7%, up from a range of 5% to 6% previously, reflecting better-than-expected second quarter results.
The Company now expects operating margin for Fiscal 2027 to expand approximately 80 to 100 basis points in constant currency, up from its prior outlook, driven primarily by gross margin expansion.
For the third quarter, the Company expects revenues to grow approximately low- to mid-single digits on a constant currency basis, centered around 3% to 4%.
The Company's full year Fiscal 2027 tax rate is still expected to be in the range of approximately 21% to 22%.
The Company continues to expect capital expenditures for Fiscal 2027 of approximately 4% to 5% of revenue.
An online archive of the broadcast will be available by accessing the Company's investor relations website at http://investor.ralphlauren.com.

Accordingly, our operating results and cash flows for the three-month and six-month periods ended September 26, 2026 are not necessarily indicative of the operating results and cash flows that may be expected for the full Fiscal 2027.

We began a multi-year global project during our fiscal year ended March 30, 2024 that is expected to significantly transform the way in which we operate our business and further enable our long-term strategic pivot towards a global direct-to-consumer-oriented model (the "Next Generation Transformation project" or "NGT project").

These efforts are expected to result in significant process improvements and the creation of synergies across core areas of operations, as well as financial planning and reporting, better enabling us to optimize inventory levels and increase the speed with which we react to changes in consumer demand across markets, among other benefits.

We continue to advance key workstreams under the NGT project including completion of global templates that support our core enterprise resource planning platform and related processes, automation of certain distribution center operations, and the global roll-out of merchandise allocation and demand planning tools.

In connection with the NGT project, we incurred other charges of $23.9 million and $44.7 million during the three-month and six-month periods ended September 26, 2026, respectively, and $25.7 million and $36.7 million during the three-month and six-month periods ended September 27, 2025, respectively.

We continue to monitor the geopolitical and macroeconomic environment and adjust our operating strategies as appropriate, while remaining focused on executing our broader long-term strategy of brand elevation, including initiatives intended to support average unit retail ("AUR") growth and brand equity.

During the three-month periods ended September 26, 2026 and September 27, 2025, we recorded net restructuring charges of $4.0 million and $9.5 million, respectively, associated with severance and benefits costs, as well as other charges of $23.9 million and $25.7 million, respectively, incurred in connection with our Next Generation Transformation project (refer to " Recent Developments " for additional discussion).

During the six-month periods ended September 26, 2026 and September 27, 2025, we recorded net restructuring charges of $7.0 million and $15.9 million, respectively, associated with severance and benefits costs, as well as other charges of $44.7 million and $36.7 million, respectively, incurred in connection with our Next Generation Transformation project (refer to " Recent Developments " for additional discussion).
